title: Let Me Not Wander Comfortless
description: Let Me Not Wander Comfortless in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 338, “Consolation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let me not wan-der com-fort-less, My Fa-ther, far from Thee; But still be-neath Thy guar-dian wing In ho-ly qui-et be.

lines: But still beneath Thy guardian wing
The storms of grief, the tears of woe,
Soothed by Thy love, shall cease;
And all the trembling spirit breathe
The power of prayer shall o'er me shed
More soft than evening's twilight dews,
My soul shall feel its balm.
For there Thy still, small voice shall speak
And tears and smiles, and grief and joy,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
